title: Bounded below injective descent and shift-compatible comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A'$ be abelian categories with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian; def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $K^+(\mathcal A)$ for the homotopy category of bounded below integer cochain complexes, $D^+(\mathcal A)$ for its localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category; def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and $K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\mathcal A)$ for the full subcategory on complexes with injective terms. Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category and let $F:K^+(\mathcal A)\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ and $F':K^+(\mathcal A')\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ be exact functors, equipped with their shift comparisons [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be additive and exact, and also write $E$ for its termwise functor and $D^+E$ for the induced derived functor. Suppose $\tau:F\Rightarrow F'E$ is a natural transformation on homotopy categories compatible with the shift comparisons.
There are exact functors $RF:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ and $RF':D^+(\mathcal A')\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ computed by applying $F,F'$ to bounded below injective representatives. For $K$, choose quasi-isomorphisms $k:K\to I$ and $k':EK\to J$ to bounded below complexes of injectives. Choose a chain map $u:EI\to J$ such that $u\circ E(k)$ and $k'$ are homotopic. The morphism represented by
$$F(I)\xrightarrow{\tau_I}F'(EI)\xrightarrow{F'(u)}F'(J)$$
defines a natural transformation $R\tau:RF\Rightarrow RF'\circ D^+E$, independent of $I,J,k,k',u$ under the canonical comparison isomorphisms. It is natural for every morphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$, including morphisms $K\to L[1]$, and commutes with the induced shift comparisons. The construction respects identity and composition of such comparison data. No assumption that $EI$ has injective terms is required.

proof.text: For every K lift the inverse counit of the injective equivalence through the same Hom bijection to obtain biAug K. The counit determines this homotopy class uniquely, and its naturality lifts to biAug. On injective objects biAug is the image of the equivalence unit. Applying F then Qh gives a natural transformation biUnit F. The injective derivability structure, furnished by bounded-below injective resolutions, identifies this as a right-derived unit; it is invertible on injectives. Naturality of biUnit and its value on injectives give biUnit(K) ≫ boundedInjectiveResolutionIso.hom = Qh(F(k)).

proof.text: Form biBeta from Qh(τ), the target biUnit and the inverse exact-E factorization. Prove that BoundedInjectiveComparison is equivalent to biUnit F ≫ whiskerLeft Qh t = biBeta. For the forward implication use the canonical augmentations biAug and the unique lift u, then cancel the target resolution isomorphism. For the reverse implication compute at an injective I, cancel the invertible unit there, and use naturality of the target unit at u, of t at Qh(k), and of the exact-E factorization. The augmentation equation E(k) ≫ u = k′ yields the required formula for arbitrary resolutions.

proof.text: The unit biUnit commutes with shifts: after restriction to injectives it is the equivalence unit whiskered with inclusion, F and Qh, with associators inserted; the equivalence unit commutes with shifts. Detect shift compatibility on injectives using biAug. The transformation biBeta commutes with shifts by composition. After restriction to injectives, whiskerLeft Qh t is the inverse of biUnit composed with biBeta, so it commutes with shifts. Detect this first on all bounded-below homotopy objects via biAug, then on all derived objects via essential surjectivity of Qh.

The unit equation and mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso_hom_app_factorsh reduce the comparison to identities. For composition data compare r followed by the derived composition isomorphism with t followed by whiskerLeft(D⁺E,s), again using rightDerived_ext. Postcompose the unit equations with the canonical E′-image factorization and target factorization. mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso_hom_app_factorsh handles r, naturality of s moves the first factorization across s, and the unit formulas for t and s identify the composite with the termwise composite datum. Specialized the existing filtered equivalence to filtration interval [0,0], then constructed the comparison via the K-injective Hom bijection and proved arbitrary-derived-morphism naturality, all choice independence, shift compatibility, and identity/composition by explicit equations. No change to the statement and no assumption that E preserves injectives.
